memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" "Here I am," he replied. - Gen 22:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Scripture tells us plainly at the outset what is happening: "God tested Abraham." We're let in on something Abraham himself did not yet know. This wasn't punishment, and it wasn't God being cruel. It was a test - designed not to make Abraham fail, but to prove and deepen a faith that was real.

We need to understand what a test from God is and isn't. God does not tempt us toward evil; "God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does he tempt anyone" (Jas 1:13). But He does sometimes test our faith, the way fire refines gold, to strengthen what is genuine and bring it to light. A tested faith becomes a stronger faith.

Notice Abraham's response to God's call: "Here I am." It is the answer of a heart ready, available, attentive. Before Abraham knows what God will ask, he makes himself available. That posture - "Here I am, Lord" - is the beginning of every faithful walk with God.

If you are in a season of testing, take heart. It does not mean God has abandoned you or is against you. "The testing of your faith produces perseverance" (Jas 1:3), and God is at work refining something precious in you. He tests those He loves, not to break them, but to build them. Can you say, even now, "Here I am, Lord" - available to Him before you even know what He will ask?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you in a season of testing? Can you trust it's meant to strengthen, not destroy?
- Can you say "Here I am" to God before knowing what He will ask?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when You test my faith, help me trust that You are refining something precious, not abandoning me. Give me a ready heart that says "Here I am" before I even know what You will ask.
Amen.
